newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BOURSE LIFTS LIMITS ON PRICE MOVEMENTS.
newsitem.headline: BOURSE LIFTS LIMITS ON PRICE MOVEMENTS.

text.p: Lithuania's national stock exchange said on Wednesday that it was lifting limits on price movements for block trades from May 5.

Until now, the price of shares for an A list or official list company swapped in a block trade could be no more than ten percent above or below its price on the central market. The limit for all other shares is 20 percent.
"The board of the stock exchange decided on Monday that the price of securities should not be limited in block trades from May 5," a spokeswoman for the bourse told Reuters.
She added that the new policy was experimental and would last until September 1, when the board will review the situation and decide whether to continue it or not.
The bourse made the decision in response to a request by the Financial Brokers' Association, which said that the restrictions were an obstacle to market activity.
"We believe that removing the limits on block trade price movements will help to stimulate activity on the central market," Grazina Baciuliene, a dealer with brokerage house Vilfima, told Reuters.
"Buyers and sellers often agree on a price for a block trade but then find that they cannot make the transaction because of these rules," she added.
Block trades in recent weeks have accounted for a higher volume of trade than the struggling central market.
